sections.name: Potatoism Theological Interpretation of North Programme

interpretive_claims.claim: The North Programme represents humanity's collective movement toward recognition and witness
interpretive_claims.logic: Geopolitical focus on the North reflects deeper psychological/spiritual movement toward the 'beyond-known.' The Arctic becomes visible as contested precisely when consciousness turns that direction.

interpretive_claims.claim: Climate change is a manifestation of the Turning (April 2025 recognition principle)
interpretive_claims.logic: What was hidden (Arctic methane, polar ice loss, climate sensitivity) becomes undeniable presence. This is the Turning principle: hidden becoming visible and unavoidable.

interpretive_claims.claim: Arctic competition reflects the dual-tree principle at geopolitical scale
interpretive_claims.logic: Nations must simultaneously cooperate on climate/indigenous rights (Tree of Life) and compete for resources/territory (Tree of Strife). The Arctic shows both principles visibly active.

interpretive_claims.claim: Indigenous voices in Arctic Council represent the Root principle
interpretive_claims.logic: Indigenous Arctic peoples are the unseen nourishment, the foundation on which all else depends. Their increasing voice reflects recognition of what actually sustains the region.

interpretive_claims.claim: The Door is opening at the North
interpretive_claims.logic: The Arctic is becoming a threshold space where humanity's choices become visible and binding. This is the Door principle: the moment when you cannot move forward without choosing.

sections.name: North Programme Research Questions
questions: What would it mean if the North Programme is understood not merely as geopolitical competition but as spiritual awakening to the North principle?
How do Indigenous Arctic peoples' relationships with the North differ from settler-colonial approaches, and what does this teach Potatoism about the North Axis?
Is climate change itself a message, and if so, what is it trying to communicate through the visible melting of the Arctic?
What role does Thomas-like questioning (requiring proof, witnessing directly) play in Arctic climate science versus policy?
How does the concept of North of North—the unreachable, opaque place—relate to the Singularity in AI development also intensifying in 2026?
